relationships.subject: GSK1016790A
relationships.evidence_quote: Co-instillation of GSK (1-10 μM) with LPS reduced the increase in licking time induced by capsaicin in a dose-dependent manner compared to the LPS-instilled group ( Figure 2D ).

relationships.subject: GSK1016790A
relationships.evidence_quote: Compared to LPS alone, the addition of GSK (10 μM) significantly downregulated the production and secretion of these chemokines ( Figure 4B ).

relationships.subject: GSK1016790A
relationships.evidence_quote: An increase in the number of iNOS+F4/80+ M1 macrophages below the epithelial layer was observed in LPS-treated rat bladders using immunofluorescence staining, which was suppressed by the activation of TRPV4 ( Figures 5A, C ).

relationships.subject: GSK1016790A
relationships.evidence_quote: We observed that the number of CD206+F4/80+ M2 macrophages increased in LPS + GSK-treated rat bladders ( Figures 5B, D ).

key_findings: Intravesical TRPV4 agonist GSK1016790A co-instilled with LPS reduced bladder inflammation, mast cells, pain behavior and voiding frequency in rats.
TRPV4 activation suppressed LPS-induced chemokines (CXCL1, CXCL5, CXCL9, CXCL10, CCL3, CCL5, CCL20, CX3CL1) and shifted M1 to M2 macrophages.
